title: The Lamp-Oil Ratio of the Drowned Stair
story: At the bottom of a flooded lighthouse stair, Harrowkelp the Stair Smotherer snuffs every flame with wet green fronds, trapping four lantern-keepers in the dark. Mr 6 finds the oil cabinet: the only mix that burns through kelp-damp must be whale-glow and ember-sap in a ratio of 5 to 3. The keepers need 48 flasks of mixed oil to light the whole stair.
question: How many flasks of whale-glow does Mr 6 need to pour?
solution: The ratio 5 to 3 means each 'batch' is 5 + 3 = 8 flasks.
Each batch has 5 flasks of whale-glow, so 6 * 5 = 30 flasks of whale-glow.
praise: Splitting the mix into ratio parts was exactly the right move — the last step was multiplying the number of batches by the 5 whale-glow shares.
hint: First find out how many flasks make up one whole 'ratio batch' of 5 parts plus 3 parts.
victory: The stair blazes gold, and Harrowkelp slithers off grumbling that nobody respects a good damp anymore. The keepers climb out and name the top step 'Sixth Landing.'
imagePrompt: A brave numeral-six knight with a blue cape holding a blazing lantern on a flooded spiral lighthouse stair, as a huge kelp-fronded sea creature recoils from the warm golden light.
